text:
sam: quick sync on last night's routing noise. lots of routes ended up with identical final scores and traffic hopped between low-capacity zones.

ivy: saw the alert. this looked like score entropy collapse after quantize + penalty. we need a stable-sort instead of falling back to list order.

jorge: agreed. summary of root cause: scoring pipeline -> winsorize -> quantize(16) -> normalize. quantize collapses small differences, then runtime picks first matching candidate.

maya: proposal: compiler emits a compact tie_key (u16) per route. runtime comparator compares lexicographic tuple: (bucket_id, cost_band, latency_band, tie_key). deterministic and cheap.

sam: +1. also add per-tenant comparator_profile to flip cost/latency order for latency-SLO tenants. must be explicit opt-in.

ivy: important: tie_key must be stable across hot reloads. suggest tie_key = low16(xxhash64(route_id) xor region_shard). bind to policy manifest so it persists until recompile.

jorge: perf note: make comparator pure integer compares on stack; represent all fields as uint16 in proto to avoid allocations. target: <250ns per decision on p99.

maya: anti-flap: when comparator chooses a node below capacity_threshold (default 12%), apply a soft hold per-tenant for 20s unless new candidate is >= 2 buckets better. prevents oscillation. record policy.flap.soft_hold metric.

sam: telemetry plan: policy.tie_resolutions.total, policy.tie_resolutions.by_breaker (bucket|cost|lat|tie_key), policy.flap.soft_hold.count, and per-tenant p95 latency delta. dashboards for trend.

ivy: test matrix: unit tests for tuple ordering, sim for prod-capture scenario (small/large/eu), bench comparator perf, migration test toggling legacy_nondet_routing.

jorge: rollout: behind ff stable_sort_tiebreak, unit+sim green, canary 1% tenants 24h -> 10% 48h -> ramp. ops escape hatch: console toggle legacy_nondet_routing per-tenant for 2w.

maya: also include a small experiment: instrument how often tie_key is the deciding factor vs. cost/lat. if tie_key dominates, maybe our bins too coarse.

sam: good call. add telemetry tag for which comparator index broke the tie. helps adjust bin_count.

ivy: bin defaults: 16, but allowed range 4..128 in policy metadata. recommend 16 for most, 32 for high-churn tenants. document guidance.

jorge: compatibility: include legacy behavior flag. default OFF for new tenants, existing tenants keep their current mode until migration. ops will get a migration checklist.

policy-bot: created issue #PLAT-1633: "stable sort tiebreaker + anti-flap rollout" and linked to the compiler and runtime repos.

maya: i'll draft the RFC addendum with comparator_spec proto and anti-flap semantics. will include pseudocode and perf targets.

sam: i'll add sim scenarios and dashboards. jorge please own compiler changes. ivy you own runtime comparator + telemetry.

jorge: will open PR with tie_key emit and proto change. include bench results.

ivy: i'll prototype comparator microbench and post numbers. aiming to keep compare cost <200ns.

maya: timeline: RFC addendum + PRs by mid-week, sims green, then canary next week.

sam: thanks all. small followup: include an enterprise opt-out note in the migration docs in case large customers rely on previous nondet behavior.

policy-bot: noted. created subtask PLAT-1633-1 for migration docs.

jorge: lgtm.

impressions: concise plan, low-risk rollout, telemetry to observe dominance.

maya: thanks — see PRs soon :shipit:
